title.narrative: IDB LAB NaturaTech LAC: Technologies for biodiversity conservation
IDB LAB NaturaTech LAC: Teknik för bevarande av biologisk mångfald

description.narrative:
The main objective is to enhance the effectiveness, scalability and transparency of biodiversity conservation contributing to climate change mitigation by supporting the development and adoption of innovative nature-based solutions (NbS) in the Latin America and Caribbean region.
This will be achieved through three components:
Component 1. Discover and support deployment: The objective of this component is to assist in the acceleration of the deployment and responsible adoption of new technologies in key application areas, as well as testing and funding of new NbS models, including new financing approaches.
Component 2. Enhance knowledge: The objective of this component is to enhance the capabilities of innovation through emerging-tech literacy programs for practitioners and other key stakeholders. For this, NaturaTech will create the NaturaTech Academy which in its initial stage includes an online open training program to enhance the technical knowledge and the understanding of opportunities that new technologies and emerging tech infrastructures bring to the conservation and restoration of biodiversity, as well as supporting a wider knowledge of the social, business, economic, and financial benefits of conservation to private and public sectors.
Component 3. Connect opportunities: The objective of this component is to connect nature tech stakeholders, through a multidisciplinary approach, to strengthen the field and foster transdisciplinary and transboundary cooperation for better flow of resources, tools, and input for enabling policies that support innovation and investments in this field.
Moreover, although Sida's funds will be instrumental for the full NaturaTech LAC Initiative, it is foreseen that some strategic activities will be co-developed both with Sida as with other Swedish institutions, such as the Stockholm Resilience Center. This collaboration with Sida and the contribution of Swedish resources to the Project includes, but is not limited to:
- Alignment with Swedish resources to enable the transfer of knowledge and lessons learned between them and LAC partners in the project, including those who implement proof of concepts. This will help reduce knowledge gaps, enable collective learning, and increase impact.
- Collaboration to leverage the expertise and resources of renowned Swedish institutions and organizations to drive the Tech for Nature-based Solutions (NbS) field in the Pan-amazon regions and overall LAC. This is via creating knowledge by including Swedish experts and practitioners in the capacity-building courses and implementation of proof of concepts.
- Integration of and collaboration with experts in Sweden in the high-level round tables on various topics such as climate, NbS, Artificial Intelligence, and digital technologies. The dialogues in these spaces will inform the development of policy briefs for LAC government institutions, among other stakeholders.

Detta handlingsdrivna initiativ kommer att syfta till att bli ett ledande regionalt program som överbryggar silos mellan framväxande teknik och bevarande och återställande av biologisk mångfald, och främjar både antagandet av digital teknik för mer effektiva, transparenta och skalbara lösningar med potential att underlätta nya marknader och innovativa finansiella instrument som drivs av naturens monetära och icke-monetära värde. Detta kommer i sin tur att minska underskottet när det gäller att testa nya tillämpningar av dessa tekniker för att tillgodose kontextbaserade behov av bevarande och förnyelse av biologisk mångfald, samtidigt som den roll som ursprungsbefolkningens traditionella kunskap spelar för en effektfull implementering och ett hållbart antagande av projektet i på lång sikt, samt förstärka gränsöverskridande samarbete och multidisciplinära samarbeten med till exempel konsoliderade Nature-based-Solutions-arbetsgrupper i Europa och andra regioner.

This action-driven initiative will aim to become a leading regional program that bridges the silos between emerging technologies and biodiversity conservation and restoration, promoting both the adoption of digital technologies for more effective, transparent, and scalable solutions with the potential to facilitate new markets and innovative financial instruments driven by the monetary and non-monetary value of nature. This will, in turn, reduce the deficit in testing new applications of these technologies to address context-based biodiversity conservation and regeneration needs, while also highlighting the role of the Indigenous People’s traditional knowledge for an impactful implementation and the sustainable adoption of the project in the long term, as well as enhancing transboundary cooperation and multidisciplinary collaborations with, for example, consolidated Nature-based-Solutions working groups in Europe and other regions.
